summary: Auto ABS delinquencies have reached levels exceeding 2008 peaks while subprime stress indicators remain elevated, warranting close monitoring across the portfolio alongside concurrent new issuance activity in solar securitizations (Sunrun $584M, Sabal $430M, Loanpal) and multiple GM Financial and AmeriCredit trust filings.

Portfolio surveillance highlights include significant rating downgrades in student loan ABS following U.S. sovereign downgrade, robust new issuance activity across auto ABS and CLOs, and multiple rating actions across credit card ABS, RMBS, and CMBS sectors.

Today's surveillance batch includes eight auto ABS new issuances (including a portfolio-match Westlake Automobile Receivables Trust 2026-1), seven solar/renewable ABS issuances alongside mixed rating actions with notable downgrades at Osprey Securitization I and Sunnova Helios, five CLO rating actions with downgrades at Battalion and Apex, five RMBS issuances and upgrades, two CMBS actions, four credit card ABS issuances, and a Fitch report on deteriorating U.S. credit card charge-off performance.

GM Financial and AmeriCredit dominate this week's surveillance batch with 13 auto ABS filings across consumer receivables and leasing trusts spanning 2023–2026 vintages, while new issuance activity includes MoneyMe's dual Australian auto ABS closings ($455.4M and $517.5M) and FleetPartners' A$400M securitization, alongside preliminary ratings on Spanish RMBS (Lugo Funding 2026-1) and UK RMBS (Turquoise VII, Eurohome 2007-1 downgrade), plus new CLO issuances rated by Fitch.

MoneyMe's $517.5 million automotive ABS issuance and $202.75 million consumer ABS performance report lead a week dominated by CLO refinancings, extensions, and new issuances across multiple managers alongside stable RMBS and CMBS market activity.
AGL CLO 2 Ltd. released its latest performance and servicer report for July 2026, showing continued portfolio monitoring activity across the CLO sector.

volume_line: 102 items today vs. 5.9/day 30-day average — busier than usual.
narrative: Targeted downgrades in UK RMBS and interest-only CMBS classes signal underlying credit stress, while robust auto ABS issuance velocity and new CLO ratings indicate continued origination momentum, suggesting the market is bifurcating between challenged legacy structured products and fresh supply.
